title: Nesting (support-aware)
learningObjectives: Explain nesting (support-aware) and use modern CSS features responsibly.

understand.concept: CSS nesting allows style rules to be nested inside a parent rule, reducing repeated selectors. The nested selector can use the ampersand (&) to refer to the parent selector. Nesting has defined parsing and specificity behaviour, so it should be used consistently.
understand.whyItMatters: Nesting can improve organisation but excessive depth makes selectors difficult to understand. Use it when related styles genuinely belong together and check compatibility for the supported browser set.
understand.analogy: Nesting is like keeping related instructions inside one labelled section rather than scattering them through a document.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; CSS parsing, specificity, and feature support follow the relevant browser standards.

explain.narrative: The heading and link rules are nested under .card, and the ampersand refers to the parent selector.

examples.explanation: The heading and link rules are nested under .card, and the ampersand refers to the parent selector.

practise.guidedTask: Rewrite a flat card stylesheet using native CSS nesting. Keep nesting shallow and compare the resulting selector relationships.
practise.independentTask: Apply the concept to a small component. Check computed styles, maintainability, and fallback behaviour where relevant.
hints: Keep selectors understandable and nesting shallow.
Use feature queries for progressive enhancement.
Inspect the actual winning rule before adding overrides.

questions.prompt: What does the ampersand represent in CSS nesting?
questions.explanation: The nesting selector (&) represents the outer selector in the nested rule.

questions.prompt: What is a good principle for maintainable modern CSS?
options: Use clear rules, appropriate fallbacks, and inspect computed behaviour
Use the newest feature everywhere without checking support
Increase specificity whenever a style does not apply
questions.answer: Use clear rules, appropriate fallbacks, and inspect computed behaviour
questions.explanation: Maintainability depends on clarity, support-aware enhancement, and understanding the cascade.
